topics.title: Checking Your Vehicle
topics.blurb: Brakes, tires, lights — what to check and how, before a problem finds you.

topics.title: When Something Fails While Driving
topics.blurb: Blowouts, brake failure, skids, stuck pedal, fire. The right reaction is often the opposite of instinct.

topics.title: If You Are in a Crash
topics.blurb: What you must do, what you must report, and what you must exchange.

concepts.label: Checking the brake pedal
concepts.statement: The brake pedal should not go more than halfway to the floor and should feel like it is hitting something hard; a spongy pedal may mean air in the brake line.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It should not go more than halfway to the floor.

concepts.label: The penny tread test
concepts.statement: Put a penny into the deepest groove with Lincoln's head first — if you can see all of his head, the tires are too worn to drive on.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Can you see all of his head?  If yes, your tires

concepts.label: Checking tire pressure
concepts.statement: Check tire pressure monthly with a gauge while the tires are cold, comparing against the PSI figure on the sticker inside the driver's door jamb.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Check tire pressure with a gauge monthly

concepts.label: Surviving a blowout
concepts.statement: In a blowout, hold the wheel tightly, steer straight ahead and ease off the accelerator — do not brake until the vehicle is under control.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: hold tightly to the steering wheel, steer straight ahead, and ease up on the accelerator.

concepts.label: What causes blowouts
concepts.statement: Under-inflated tires are one of the most common causes of blowouts.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Under-inflated tires are one of the most common causes of blowouts

concepts.label: If the brakes fail
concepts.statement: Pump the brake pedal quickly, shift to a lower gear, warn others with horn and lights, and use the parking brake while holding the release.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Shift to a lower gear and look for a place to slow down and stop off the roadway.

concepts.label: Steering out of a skid
concepts.statement: In a skid, take your foot off the gas and turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid; do not brake unless you are in danger of hitting something.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.

concepts.label: Overheating engine
concepts.statement: If the engine overheats, pull off the road and turn it off — do not remove the radiator cap until the engine has cooled.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not remove the radiator cap until the engine has cooled off.

concepts.label: Stuck gas pedal
concepts.statement: If the gas pedal sticks, keep steering and watching the road, try to free it with your foot, then push in the clutch or shift to neutral before braking to a safe stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If this does not work, push in the clutch or shift into neutral.

concepts.label: Wheels off the pavement
concepts.statement: If your wheels drop off the road, grip the wheel, stay on the shoulder, ease off the accelerator and slow gradually before turning back onto the pavement.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Stay on the shoulder and ease off the accelerator.

concepts.label: Vehicle fire
concepts.statement: Smother a vehicle fire with dirt or sand, never water, because burning gasoline floats on water and spreads the fire; if it gets out of control move at least 100 feet away.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not use water because burning gasoline will float on water and spread the fire.

concepts.label: Headlight failure
concepts.statement: If your headlights fail on a dark highway, try parking lights, turn signals or emergency flashers and get off the roadway; if all lights fail, stay on the roadway and slow down enough to pull off safely.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If all lights fail, stay on the roadway and slow down enough

concepts.label: Stop and secure the scene
concepts.statement: If you are involved in a crash, stop immediately, turn off the ignition to prevent fire, and protect the scene to prevent further crashes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: If You are Involved In A Crash
source.sourceQuote: Turn off the ignition to prevent the danger of fire.

concepts.label: Reporting a crash
concepts.statement: A crash causing injury or death, or property damage of $1,000 or more, must be reported to the nearest law enforcement agency.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: If You are Involved In A Crash
source.sourceQuote: you must notify the nearest law enforcement agency.

concepts.label: Information to exchange
concepts.statement: Drivers involved in a crash should exchange name, address, license plate number and motor vehicle insurance information.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: If You are Involved In A Crash
source.sourceQuote: The following information should be exchanged by persons involved in traffic crashes

concepts.label: Striking an unattended vehicle
concepts.statement: If you strike an unattended vehicle, try to find the owner; if you cannot, leave a written notice with your name, address, plate number, insurance information and the circumstances.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you strike an unattended vehicle, try to locate

concepts.label: Do not stop at other crashes
concepts.statement: Do not stop at a crash scene unless you are involved or can render assistance — unnecessary stopping creates additional hazards.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop at a crash scene unless you are

concepts.label: First aid priority order
concepts.statement: Give first aid in this order: control bleeding, restore breathing, treat for shock, protect broken bones — and do not move the victim unless there is danger of further injury.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Stay calm and do not move the victim unless there is danger of further injury.

concepts.label: Good Samaritan law
concepts.statement: Anyone who in good faith gives emergency care at a crash scene without pay is not liable for civil damages for any act or omission in giving that care.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: care at the scene of a crash, without pay, is liable for any civil damages

lessons.title: Checking Your Vehicle Before It Fails

rules.text: The brake pedal should not go more than halfway to the floor, and should feel like it is hitting something hard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It should not go more than halfway to the floor.

rules.text: Check tire pressure monthly with a gauge, while the tires are cold, against the PSI on the door jamb sticker.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Check tire pressure with a gauge monthly

rules.text: Test tread with a penny, head first into the deepest groove. If you can see all of Lincoln's head, the tires are too worn to drive on.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Can you see all of his head?  If yes, your tires

lessons.plainEnglish: Most roadside emergencies announce themselves beforehand if anyone is checking. A brake pedal that sinks past halfway, or feels soft instead of firm, is telling you there is air or a leak in the system. Tires that are low on air or tread are the ones that blow out. None of these checks need tools beyond a tire gauge and a penny.
lessons.whyItMatters: The handbook puts vehicle checks at the start of the emergency chapter for a reason: the cheapest way to handle a blowout or brake failure is to find the problem in a driveway instead of at 55 mph. Under-inflated tires are specifically named as one of the most common causes of blowouts.
lessons.example: Once a month you press the brake pedal before starting off and it feels firm and stops well short of halfway. You check the four tires cold with a gauge against the number on the door jamb sticker, and drop a penny into the tread. Two minutes, and you have ruled out the two failures most likely to put you off the road.

lessons.title: When Something Fails at Speed

rules.text: Blowout: hold the wheel tightly, steer straight ahead, ease off the accelerator, and do not brake until the vehicle is under control.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not brake until the vehicle is under control.

rules.text: Skid: take your foot off the gas and turn the wheel in the direction of the skid. Do not brake unless you are in danger of hitting something.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not use your brakes unless you are in danger of hitting

rules.text: Fire: smother it with dirt or sand, never water, and move at least 100 feet away if it gets out of control.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: move at least 100 feet away from the vehicle since the gas tank may explode.

lessons.plainEnglish: In almost every sudden failure, the instinct is to hit the brakes — and in most of them, braking first is the wrong move. A blowout has already made the car unstable; braking makes it worse, so you steer straight and let it slow itself before you brake. In a skid, braking locks you into the slide; you lift off the gas and steer where you want to go. The pattern to remember is: get control first, then slow down.
lessons.whyItMatters: These are the situations where you get one attempt and no time to think it through. The handbook's instructions are counter-intuitive on purpose, which is exactly why they have to be learned in advance rather than worked out at the time.
lessons.example: Your right front tire blows on a 55 mph road. The car pulls hard right. You grip the wheel firmly, steer straight rather than yanking left, and lift off the accelerator without touching the brake. As the car slows and steadies, you brake gently and pull all the way off into a safe area.

lessons.title: Your Duties at a Crash

rules.text: Stop immediately, turn off the ignition to prevent fire, and protect the scene to prevent further crashes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: If You are Involved In A Crash
source.sourceQuote: Turn off the ignition to prevent the danger of fire.

rules.text: Report a crash involving injury, death, or property damage of $1,000 or more to the nearest law enforcement agency.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: If You are Involved In A Crash
source.sourceQuote: you must notify the nearest law enforcement agency.

rules.text: Do not move an injured person unless absolutely necessary; give first aid in the order bleeding, breathing, shock, broken bones.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Stay calm and do not move the victim unless there is danger of further injury.

lessons.plainEnglish: Your duties run in order: stop, make the scene safe, help the injured, then deal with paperwork. Turning off the ignition is first because fire is the danger that turns a survivable crash into a fatal one. Moving an injured person is the most common well-meant mistake — unless they are in danger where they lie, leave them and send for help. Then exchange name, address, plate number and insurance details, and report it if anyone was hurt or damage reaches $1,000.
lessons.whyItMatters: Failing to report a qualifying crash or leaving without exchanging information is not a paperwork slip; it is an offence. And the Good Samaritan law exists so that fear of being sued is not a reason to stand back — someone giving emergency care in good faith, without pay, is not liable for civil damages.
lessons.example: You rear-end someone at a light. Nobody seems hurt, but both bumpers are wrecked and a repair will clearly run past $1,000. You stop, switch off the ignition, check on the other driver, exchange name, address, plate number and insurance, and call the nearest law enforcement agency because the damage crosses the reporting threshold.

questions.question: Your tire blows out at highway speed. What should you do first?
choices: Hold the wheel tightly, steer straight ahead, and ease up on the accelerator
Brake hard immediately to slow down as fast as possible
Steer sharply onto the shoulder straight away
Pull the parking brake to stop the vehicle quickly
questions.explanation: A blowout has already upset the car's balance, and braking makes it worse. The handbook says to hold tightly to the steering wheel, steer straight ahead and ease up on the accelerator, and not to brake until the vehicle is under control. Only then pull all the way off the road.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: hold tightly to the steering wheel, steer straight ahead, and ease up on the accelerator.

questions.question: When may you brake after a blowout?
choices: Not until the vehicle is under control
Immediately, as hard as possible
Only once you have already left the roadway
Only after shifting into neutral
questions.explanation: The handbook is explicit: do not brake until the vehicle is under control. Braking while the car is still unstable from a blown tire can turn a recoverable situation into a loss of control. Get it straight and slowed first, then brake and pull off.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not brake until the vehicle is under control.

questions.question: What does the handbook name as one of the most common causes of blowouts?
choices: Under-inflated tires
Driving with the windows down at speed
Braking too gently
Overfilled engine oil
questions.explanation: Under-inflated tires are specifically named as one of the most common causes of blowouts, which is why the handbook tells you to check tire pressure with a gauge monthly. It is the clearest link between a routine check and a dangerous failure.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Under-inflated tires are one of the most common causes of blowouts

questions.question: A driver checks tire pressure monthly. Which emergency is that habit most directly guarding against?
choices: A blowout
Brake failure
An overheating engine
Headlight failure
questions.explanation: The handbook links these directly: under-inflated tires are one of the most common causes of blowouts, so checking pressure with a gauge monthly is the routine that prevents them. The other failures listed have their own separate checks.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: so be sure to check your tires for air often.

questions.question: The rear of your vehicle begins skidding to the right. Which way do you turn the steering wheel?
choices: To the right — turn in the direction of the skid
To the left — turn against the skid
Hold the wheel perfectly straight
Turn left and brake firmly at the same time
questions.explanation: The handbook says to turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid: if the rear is skidding right, turn right. The vehicle may then begin to skid the other way, and you again turn the wheels in the direction you want to go before straightening up.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the right, turn to the

questions.question: Which action should you avoid while your vehicle is skidding?
choices: Using the brakes, unless you are in danger of hitting something
Taking your foot off the gas pedal
Turning the wheel in the direction of the skid
Staying calm and concentrating on steering
questions.explanation: The handbook says not to use your brakes unless you are in danger of hitting something, and to concentrate on steering out of trouble instead. The other three are exactly what it tells you to do: stay calm, lift off the gas, and steer in the direction of the skid.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not use your brakes unless you are in danger of hitting

questions.question: Your brakes fail while driving. What does the handbook tell you to do?
choices: Pump the brake pedal quickly, shift to a lower gear, and use the parking brake while holding the release
Switch off the ignition immediately to stop the engine
Steer into a ditch at the first opportunity
Shift into a higher gear and coast until the vehicle stops
questions.explanation: The handbook lists pumping the pedal quickly, shifting to a lower gear while looking for a place to stop off the roadway, warning others with horn and lights, and using the parking brake while holding the release so you can ease off if the rear wheels lock and cause a skid.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Pump the brake pedal quickly.

questions.question: Why does the handbook say to hold the brake release while applying the parking brake during brake failure?
choices: So you can ease up if the rear wheels lock and cause a skid
So the parking brake applies more force
So the brake lights stay illuminated
So the transmission shifts down automatically
questions.explanation: Holding the release lets you back off instantly. The handbook gives the reason directly: if the rear wheels lock they will cause a skid, and being able to ease up prevents trading a braking problem for a loss of control.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Use the parking brake, but hold the brake release so you can ease up on the brake if the rear wheels lock and

questions.question: Why should you not use water on a burning vehicle?
choices: Burning gasoline floats on water, which spreads the fire
Water damages the engine block permanently
Water conducts electricity from the battery
Water causes the tires to explode
questions.explanation: The handbook gives this exact reason: do not use water because burning gasoline will float on water and spread the fire. If no chemical fire extinguisher is available, smother the fire with dirt or sand instead.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not use water because burning gasoline will float on water and spread the fire.

questions.question: A vehicle fire is getting out of control. How far away should you move?
choices: At least 100 feet, because the gas tank may explode
About 20 feet, far enough to avoid the smoke
Just outside the vehicle is sufficient
At least half a mile
questions.explanation: The handbook says to move at least 100 feet away from the vehicle since the gas tank may explode. Standing just clear of the car is not enough once a fire is beyond control.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: move at least 100 feet away from the vehicle since the gas tank may explode.

questions.question: Your temperature warning light comes on. What should you do?
choices: Pull off the road, turn the engine off, and leave the radiator cap alone until it cools
Keep driving to the nearest service station regardless of distance
Remove the radiator cap at once to release pressure
Turn the heater off and continue at highway speed
questions.explanation: The handbook says to pull off the road and turn the engine off, and not to remove the radiator cap until the engine has cooled off. Removing the cap from a hot system releases scalding coolant under pressure.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not remove the radiator cap until the engine has cooled off.

questions.question: How does the handbook suggest preventing overheating in slow-moving traffic?
choices: Shift into neutral and race the engine briefly during stops to speed up the fan and water pump
Switch the engine off at every stop
Drive in the highest gear available
Open the hood while stopped in traffic
questions.explanation: The handbook describes shifting into neutral and racing the engine briefly during stops, which speeds up the fan and water pump and moves more air and coolant through the system while the vehicle is not moving fast enough to do it naturally.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You can prevent overheating in slow-moving traffic by shifting into neutral and racing your engine

questions.question: Your gas pedal sticks down. After trying to free it with your foot, what does the handbook say to do next?
choices: Push in the clutch or shift into neutral
Turn off the ignition immediately while still at speed
Apply the parking brake at full force
Steer onto the shoulder without slowing
questions.explanation: The order matters. Concentrate on steering and keep your eyes on the road, try to free the pedal with your foot, and if that does not work push in the clutch or shift into neutral. Only then use the brakes, stop at the nearest safe place, and turn off the ignition.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If this does not work, push in the clutch or shift into neutral.

questions.question: When should the ignition be turned off if the gas pedal sticks?
choices: After braking and stopping at the nearest safe place
Immediately, before doing anything else
As soon as the clutch is pushed in
Never — the ignition should be left running
questions.explanation: The handbook puts turning off the ignition last: use your brakes, stop at the nearest safe place, and turn off the ignition. Killing the engine while still moving can cost you power steering and power brakes at the worst moment.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Use your brakes, stop at the nearest safe place, and turn off the ignition.

questions.question: Your right wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder. What should you do?
choices: Grip the wheel, stay on the shoulder, ease off the accelerator and slow gradually before returning
Steer back onto the pavement immediately at the same speed
Brake hard while turning sharply back onto the road
Accelerate to regain stability before steering back
questions.explanation: The handbook says to grip the steering wheel tightly, stay on the shoulder, ease off the accelerator, brake gently and slow gradually. Only after the speed is reduced, and after checking traffic behind and ahead, do you turn the wheels sharply back onto the pavement.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Stay on the shoulder and ease off the accelerator.

questions.question: Once back on the pavement after running off the road, why does the handbook say to turn the wheels the other way immediately?
choices: To keep the vehicle from heading across the highway
To straighten the tires and reduce wear
To signal other drivers that you have recovered
To engage the anti-lock braking system
questions.explanation: You turn sharply to climb the pavement edge, which means the wheels are pointed across the road. The handbook says that as soon as the wheels hit the edge of the pavement you turn them the other way to keep the vehicle from heading across the highway into oncoming traffic.

source.sourceQuote: turn them the other way to keep your vehicle from heading

questions.question: Your headlights fail completely on a dark highway and no other lights work. What does the handbook advise?
choices: Stay on the roadway and slow down enough to pull off the roadway safely
Stop immediately in the travel lane
Speed up to reach the next lit area quickly
Steer off the road instantly without slowing
questions.explanation: If all lights fail, the handbook says to stay on the roadway and slow down enough to pull off safely. Before that, you would try parking lights, direction signals or emergency flashers — anything that makes you visible while you get clear.

questions.question: Which lights does the handbook suggest trying if your headlights fail on a dark highway?
choices: Parking lights, direction signals, or emergency flashers
Interior dome lights only
High beams only
The brake lights held on with the pedal
questions.explanation: The handbook names parking lights, direction signals and emergency flashers as the fallbacks to try while getting off the roadway. The goal is to remain visible to other traffic, which dome lights and held brake lights do not reliably achieve.

questions.question: How far should the brake pedal travel when you press it during a check?
choices: Not more than halfway to the floor
All the way to the floor
About three-quarters of the way down
It should not move at all
questions.explanation: The handbook says the pedal should not go more than halfway to the floor and should feel like it is hitting something hard. A spongy feel suggests air bubbles in the brake line, and a pedal that keeps sinking suggests a leak in the braking system.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It should not go more than halfway to the floor.

questions.question: Your brake pedal feels spongy rather than firm. What does the handbook say this may indicate?
choices: Air bubbles in the brake line
Tires that are over-inflated
A parking brake that needs adjustment
Low windshield washer fluid
questions.explanation: A spongy pedal suggests air bubbles in the brake line. The related test is to push down and count to ten — if the pedal keeps going down, there may be a leak in the braking system. Both are reasons to have the brakes looked at before driving.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If it feels spongy, air bubbles may be in the brake line.

questions.question: You put a penny head-first into your tire's deepest groove and can see all of Lincoln's head. What does that mean?
choices: The tires are too worn — do not drive on them and get them replaced
The tread depth is ideal
The tire is over-inflated
The tire needs rotating but is safe to use
questions.explanation: Seeing all of Lincoln's head means there is not enough tread left. The handbook's instruction is direct: your tires are too worn, do not drive on them, and make sure to get them replaced. Tread depth is what lets a tire clear water and grip.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Can you see all of his head?  If yes, your tires

questions.question: When should tire pressure be measured for an accurate reading?
choices: When the tires are cold
Immediately after a long drive
Only when the tires look visibly low
After driving at least 20 miles to warm them
questions.explanation: The handbook says to make sure you check when they are cold, and to compare the gauge reading against the PSI number on the sticker inside the door jamb. Driving heats the air inside a tire and raises the reading, which hides a tire that is actually low.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: make sure you check when they are cold

questions.question: Where does the handbook say to find the correct tire pressure for your vehicle?
choices: On a sticker on the inside of the driver's door jamb
Moulded into the sidewall of each tire
On the underside of the fuel filler cap
Stamped on the wheel rim
questions.explanation: The handbook says to open your car door and look on the inside jamb for a sticker showing the PSI, then compare your gauge reading against that number — letting air out if too high, adding air if too low.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Open your car door, on the inside jamb, you should see a sticker.

questions.question: You are involved in a crash. Why does the handbook say to turn off the ignition?
choices: To prevent the danger of fire
To preserve the battery for emergency calls
To stop the odometer recording further miles
Because the law requires the engine to be off before exchanging details
questions.explanation: The handbook gives the reason directly: turn off the ignition to prevent the danger of fire. It comes under step one, stop immediately, alongside protecting the scene with flares, a flagman or other means to prevent further crashes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: Which crash must be reported to the nearest law enforcement agency?
choices: One causing injury or death, or property damage of $1,000 or more
Only one where someone is taken to hospital
Only one involving three or more vehicles
Any crash of any kind, without exception
questions.explanation: The handbook sets the threshold at a crash resulting in injury or death of any person, or property damage of $1,000 or more. Below that threshold and with no injuries there is no duty to notify, though you still exchange information with the other driver.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: If You are Involved In A Crash

questions.question: Which information should drivers exchange after a traffic crash?
choices: Name, address, license plate number and motor vehicle insurance information
Name and phone number only
Driver's license number and date of birth only
Employer details and vehicle purchase price
questions.explanation: The handbook lists exactly four items to exchange: name, address, license plate number, and motor vehicle insurance information. The same four, plus the circumstances of the crash, go on a written notice if you strike an unattended vehicle and cannot find the owner.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: You back into a parked car in a lot and cannot find the owner. What must you do?
choices: Leave a written notice with your name, address, plate number, insurance information and the circumstances
Leave the scene, since no one was present to be harmed
Report it only if the damage exceeds $5,000
Leave a note with your phone number only
questions.explanation: The handbook says to try to locate the owner, and if that is not possible to leave a written notice containing your name, address, license plate number, motor vehicle insurance information and the circumstances of the crash. Driving away without doing so is leaving the scene.

questions.question: You drive past a crash that is already being attended to and you cannot offer any help. What does the handbook say?
choices: Do not stop — unnecessary stopping creates additional hazards at the scene
Always stop, as every driver has a duty to remain
Stop only if you have a camera to document it
Stop and direct traffic yourself
questions.explanation: The handbook's crash rule says not to stop at a crash scene unless you are involved or can render assistance, because unnecessary stopping creates additional hazards. Spectator traffic blocks emergency vehicles and causes secondary collisions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: In what order does the handbook say to give first aid at a crash?
choices: Control bleeding, restore breathing, treat for shock, protect broken bones
Protect broken bones, treat for shock, control bleeding, restore breathing
Restore breathing, protect broken bones, control bleeding, treat for shock
Treat for shock, control bleeding, protect broken bones, restore breathing
questions.explanation: The handbook numbers them: control bleeding, restore breathing, treat for shock, protect broken bones. It also says to stay calm, keep the victim lying down and comfortable, and not to move them unless there is danger of further injury.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: When should you move an injured person at a crash scene?
choices: Only when there is danger of further injury if they stay where they are
Always, to get them clear of the vehicle
Whenever they ask to be moved
Only after law enforcement arrives
questions.explanation: The handbook says to stay calm and not move the victim unless there is danger of further injury, and elsewhere that the injured should not be moved unless absolutely necessary. Moving someone with a spinal injury can cause permanent harm, so the default is to leave them and send for aid.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Stay calm and do not move the victim unless there is danger of further injury.

questions.question: Under West Virginia's Good Samaritan law, who is protected from civil liability for giving emergency care at a crash?
choices: Anyone who gives emergency care in good faith without pay, including doctors and dentists
Only licensed physicians
Only certified emergency medical personnel
Nobody — anyone who intervenes accepts full liability
questions.explanation: The handbook states that no one, including those licensed to practice medicine or dentistry, who in good faith gives emergency care at the scene of a crash without pay is liable for civil damages as a result of any act or omission in giving that care. The protection is broad and deliberate, so fear of liability does not stop people helping.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the handbook's steps when you are involved in a crash?
choices: Move all vehicles off the road before anything else so traffic can pass
Stop immediately
Protect the scene to prevent further crashes
Render aid to the injured
questions.explanation: The handbook's steps are to stop immediately and turn off the ignition, protect the scene using flares, a flagman or other means, and render aid to the injured while sending for an ambulance or law enforcement. Clearing the road for traffic is not among them, and moving the injured is specifically discouraged.

questions.question: Two cars collide with no injuries and about $300 of damage. Is notifying law enforcement required?
choices: No — the threshold is injury, death, or property damage of $1,000 or more
Yes — every crash must be reported regardless of damage
Yes — any crash involving two or more vehicles must be reported
No — crashes never need to be reported if nobody is injured
questions.explanation: The reporting duty is triggered by injury or death of any person, or property damage of $1,000 or more. At $300 with no injuries none of those apply, though the drivers should still exchange name, address, plate number and insurance information.

A quarter, placed edge-first across the tread
A dime, laid flat across the tread blocks
A nickel, inserted into the shallowest groove
questions.explanation: The handbook describes holding a penny with Lincoln's body between thumb and forefinger and placing his head first into the deepest-looking groove. If all of his head is visible the tread is too worn and the tires need replacing.

choices: Name, address, license plate number and insurance information
Nothing — a phone number is sufficient
Their date of birth and employer
A signed written statement admitting fault
questions.explanation: The handbook lists four items that should be exchanged: name, address, license plate number and motor vehicle insurance information. A phone number alone leaves you unable to trace the vehicle or make an insurance claim.

Leave a written notice immediately without looking for anyone
Drive to the nearest police station
Wait 24 hours before taking any action
questions.explanation: The handbook says to try to locate the owner first. Leaving a written notice with your name, address, plate number, insurance information and the circumstances is the fallback for when the owner cannot be found, not the first resort.

questions.question: Why does the handbook discourage stopping at a crash you are not involved in?
choices: Unnecessary stopping creates additional hazards at the scene
It is illegal to stop on any road shoulder
Insurance companies treat it as an admission of involvement
It delays the drivers behind you, which is a moving violation
questions.explanation: The handbook's stated reason is that unnecessary stopping creates additional hazards at the scene. Extra stopped vehicles block emergency access and raise the risk of secondary crashes. Stopping is appropriate only if you are involved or can render assistance.

questions.question: A bystander gives first aid at a crash and is later sued for making the injury worse. Under the Good Samaritan law, what applies?
choices: They are not liable for civil damages if they acted in good faith and without pay
They are fully liable because they are not medically trained
They are liable unless a doctor supervised them
The law protects only paid emergency responders
questions.explanation: The handbook states that no one who in good faith gives emergency care at the scene of a crash, without pay, is liable for civil damages as the result of any act or omission in giving that care. The protection covers ordinary bystanders as well as medical professionals.
